description: Wallpaper-group pattern research. 17 mathematical tilings of the 2D plane — the algebraic vocabulary of textiles, tiles, and wallpaper across all cultures. DNA = group × motif_seed × palette × tile_size. Same motif through different groups produces different symmetry worlds.

configs.notes: Group p1 — translation only, no symmetry. Simplest wallpaper group. Bauhaus palette reveals the raw motif repeating.
Group p2 — 180° rotation centers. Escher's simplest symmetry. Monochrome palette emphasizes figure-ground flipping.
Group p4m — 90° rotation + reflections. The Alhambra's most common group. Dot motif with alhambra palette reads as ceramic tilework.
Group p6m — 60° rotation + reflections. Hexagonal symmetry, richest of all 17 groups. Persian palette evokes carpet medallions.
Group p3 — 120° rotation only, no reflection. Triangular lattice with chirality. Memphis palette gives '80s postmodern textile.
Group pmm — two perpendicular reflections. Rectangular lattice. Tatami palette reads as Japanese straw weave.
Group p4g — 90° rotation + reflections NOT through centers. Subtler than p4m. Pastel palette softens the chirality.
Group p6 — 60° rotation only, no reflection. Hexagonal chirality. Monochrome reduces to pure geometry.
Group pgg — two perpendicular glides, no reflection. Chiral zig-zag. Bauhaus palette.
Group p3m1 — 120° rotation + reflection type 1. Triangular lattice with mirror lines through rotation centers. Classic Moorish tessellation.
